newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SHK Prop to spend HK$8 bln on land.
newsitem.headline: SHK Prop to spend HK$8 bln on land.

text.p: Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd has said it would spend about HK$8 billion on land acquisitions and premium payments in its financial year to June, the South China Morning Post newspaper reported on Friday.
But that was only a preliminary figure which had not been finalised, it quoted executive director Michael Wong as saying.
Wong said the company could reap more than HK$10 billion if all units in its major residential developments were sold.
But he did not provide a timeframe or a full list of the group's major residential projects.
He added Sun Hung Kai Properties was in a strong financial position with a gearing of less than 10 percent and had no plans to raise funds from the stock market, the Post said.
Properties expected to be completed this year would amount to 4.9 million square feet of which 4.3 million square feet would be for sale.
Wong said in the 1998 financial year, completed properties should amount to 6.4 million sq ft of which 4.5 million sq ft -- mostly residential space -- would be for sale, the Post said.
The official was not immediately available for comment. But a company spokeswoman confirmed the accuracy of the remarks.
